newsitem.title: UK: UK bank lending rises 3.934 billion stg in June.
newsitem.headline: UK bank lending rises 3.934 billion stg in June.

text.p: Total sterling lending by major British banks to the UK private sector rose a seasonally adjusted 3.934 billion stg in June, the British Bankers' Association said.
This compared with a May increase of 3.432 billion and the underlying six monthly average of around 2.730 billion.
Mortgage lending rose by 905 million stg compared with a May figure of 818 million and a six-monthly average of 771 million.
Tim Sweeney, director general of the BBA, said the appreciable strengthening in mortgage lending in June provided further evidence of the housing market recovery.
"The rise in lending was about 17 percent above the recent monthly average and the largest increase recorded for four years, though no doubt influenced by pre-budget activity," he said.
Consumer credit remained buoyant in June, rising by 526 million stg compared with a 595 million rise in May and a six-monthly average of 469 million.

"With industry and commerce repaying funds over the month, an increase in demand for finance by companies in the financial sector (largely through repos) was the other factor behind the growth in the major banks' lending in June," Sweeney said.
Lending to the financial sector rose by 358 million stg in June, the smallest increase so far in 1997.
Lending to manufacturing industry fell by 299 million stg. Within this, the "other manufacturing" sector repaid 147 million stg, reversing the rise seen in May.
Individuals increased their borrowing by a record 1.431 billion stg in June compared with 1.410 billion in May.
Within the financial sector, notable rises were recorded by leasing companies (467 million stg), securities dealers (425 million) and insurance companies and pension funds (241 million).
Companies in the "other financial" sector repaid 668 million stg, largely a repayment associated with the disposal of a subsidiary, and building societies repaid 113 million.
